correctness.rationale: The exact statistic (4) and Theorem 2.1 in arXiv:2007.02596 are matched with divisor-n covariance and theoretical Gaussian CF. Centered Gaussian data give Gram nP for Haar rank-d projection in 1^perp. The fixed-coordinate and difference leverage Z are Beta(d/2,(n-d-1)/2), or identically one if n=d+1. Conditional rotational invariance plus trace P=d gives E[Q|Z]=(d-Z)/(n-2), hence E[Y_i^T Y_j|Z]=(d-(n+1)Z)/2; substituting diagonal and cross terms proves all three formula terms. At n=d+1, P=I-11^T/n makes T deterministic. Packaged verify.py passes 101 beta integral, boundary, and Monte Carlo comparisons; these finite tests do not establish the universal theorem.

originality.rationale: The arXiv v1 2007.02596, Theorem 2.1 gives the exact statistic and Theorem 3.3 computes E[T_infinity,a], not E_0[T_n,a]. value.rationale: Finite Gaussian-null centering is a natural missing calibration quantity for the specific Fourier–Stein normality test. The source provides a limiting-null mean and simulation-based finite critical values, not a finite-n exact mean; at n=5,d=2,a=1 the exact value 1.45826184 differs by about 17.5% from the limiting 1.76714587. The analytic Haar-projection reduction yields the entire parameter family and the deterministic n=d+1 boundary, while making no unjustified claim about exact quantiles or full distributions.
